input.reasoning_summary: Upon reconsideration with the quantitative evidence, the claim is SUPPORTED. The gross margin declined 3.9 percentage points (from 75.0% to 71.1%) in fiscal 2026. Evidence E6 explicitly states the H20-related charges had a 2.6% unfavorable impact on gross margin. This means the H20 charges accounted for approximately 67% of the total decline (2.6/3.9 = 0.67), which reasonably supports the characterization that H20 charges were the "main" cause. The remaining ~1.3 percentage points would be attributable to the business model transition from Hopper to Blackwell. While E5 uses "also" to describe the H20 impact, the quantitative evidence shows H20 was indeed the larger contributor. The filing does not quantify the business model transition impact separately, but the explicit 2.6% figure for H20 out of a 3.9% total decline provides sufficient support for the claim that H20 charges were "mainly" responsible for the gross margin decline.
